root_idea.summary: The root has two attested semantic axes: yieldingness, humility, and servitude on the one hand, and strength or hardness on the other.
root_idea.development: The first axis develops from the status of a slave or subject into worship, humble obedience, devotion, enslavement, and the making of things tractable or well-trodden. The second axis yields strength, solidity, anger, and disdain-related usages.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The feminine active-participle form is a grammatical counterpart of عَابِد and is presented under the singular participial headword.

senses.definition: To worship, serve, or adore a deity, especially through humble and submissive obedience.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quran with God, false gods, or the Devil as object. The active, imperative, imperfect, perfect, and passive forms are grammatical variants of this lexical use; the passive means “be worshipped.”

senses.definition: In an alternate Quranic reading, to become an object of worship.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an explicitly reported alternative interpretation of a Quranic expression; the cited historical Lane reference is not converted here into a modern verse location.

senses.definition: To enslave someone or make someone as a slave; to bring someone under servile submission.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence refers to enslaving or subjugating people. The causative force includes reducing someone to the condition or work of a slave.

senses.definition: A worshipper, devotee, or one who serves a deity with devotion.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran includes masculine and feminine forms. The object may be God or, by secondary application, an idol or other deity; the feminine form عَابِدَات is included here.

senses.definition: One who rejects, disdains, or angrily repudiates a claim.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a reported interpretation of the Quranic expression in which العابدين is variously explained as worshippers, angry rejecters, scorners, or deniers. The interpretive alternatives are not treated as a settled restriction on the ordinary participle.

senses.definition: A slave or bondman; a person in a legally enslaved condition.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic legal usage includes the contrast between a slave and a free person. In the evidence, عَبِيد is associated with owned slaves, while عِبَاد commonly denotes servants or worshippers; عَبِيد with a divine genitive can nevertheless be broader.

senses.definition: A created being under God's lordship, coming to Him as a servant.
senses.usage_conditions: This sense concerns the relation established by creation and divine ownership, not necessarily a person's voluntary devotional practice.

senses.definition: A servant or worshipper devoted to God through service, obedience, and worship.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran applies this to prophets, righteous servants, and God's devoted people. عِبَاد commonly functions as its plural in this devotional sense, while the broader divine designation may also include all created beings.

senses.definition: Worship, devotional service, or humble obedience rendered to God or a deity.
senses.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the practice or act of worship, including obedience with humility and submissiveness. In the Quran-focused distinction, it is associated with doing what God approves rather than merely recognizing or approving what He does.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be excited against someone in order to annoy, molest, harm, or hurt him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction with بِهِ is reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withhold or keep someone away from another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression مَا عَبَدَكَ عَنِّي, “what has withheld you from me?”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become a slave or enter a state of slavery.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This stative verb is distinct from the Form I verb meaning worship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become angry or remain angry with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may be construed with عَلَى or, in poetic usage, transitively without a preposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To disdain, scorn, or regard something as beneath one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated noun عَبَدَة can denote intense disdain or scorn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deny, disavow, or reject an assertion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a reported lexical extension distinct from ordinary worship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To repent and blame oneself for negligence or failure to do what was required.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested as a distinct emotional and moral use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mourn, grieve, or be sorrowful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Arabic emotional usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be covetous or inordinately desirous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence treats this as a distinct use from anger and worship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cling or adhere inseparably to something or someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The prepositional construction بِهِ is required in the cited use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to become affected with mange or scab.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reports include severe or incurable mange and the resulting loss of hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render a camel submissive, tractable, or manageable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form II use applied to a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a road or path even and easy to travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use applied to a route or track.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To depart in fright, run away at random, or hasten repeatedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an intransitive Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Not to delay or be slow to do something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed construction meaning that an action was undertaken without delay.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect oneself with others or assemble together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in a Form IV plural expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a group to gather against and beat a man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction combines assembly with collective assault.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a riding camel to become exhausted, fail, perish, fall ill, or stop its rider.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive Form IV construction, also explained as a transposed form of أُبْدِعَ بِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become or make oneself a servant of God and devote oneself to religious exercises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes applying oneself to acts of devotion and following Islam as one's religion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to become refractory and difficult to manage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-related Form V usage, compared with a wild animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To call or invite someone to obedience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form V construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive a camel until it becomes fatigued and must stop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or transitive Form V construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a people to go away in parties in every direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A special Form II lexical family related to عَبَادِيدُ, not a Quranic form group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ignoble, base-born, or of low status.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported tropical application contrasting with حُرّ in the sense of noble or well-born.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sweet-smelling plant favored by camels and said to increase their milk and fatten them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun unrelated to the ordinary slave or worship branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short, broad blade, arrowhead, spearhead, or similar point.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for a weapon or tool head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In later common usage, a male black slave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a historical usage distinction reported alongside مَمْلُوك for a male white slave; it is not imposed as a restriction on Quranic عَبْد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strength, solidity, fatness, or lasting durability.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a strong, substantial garment or a strong, well-fleshed she-camel; the same branch can denote continuance or durability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone used for bruising or pounding perfume.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun distinct from the abstract sense of strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A designation of certain superior, relatively heavy dirhams.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective used in the expression الدَّرَاهِمُ العَبْدِيَّةُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of melon associated with Egypt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A post-Classical botanical name associated with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vacant, desolate, or waterless desert or tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is also used as a proper-name designation for the desert.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great calamity or disastrous situation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative proverbial use derived from the image of a desolate desert inhabited by hissing serpents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person devoted to serving and attending to worldly possessions or desires.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical ethical extension, as in “servant of the dirham” or “servant of the dinar”; it is not assigned as a Quranic sense here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion or appendage of the stomach of a ruminant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also called فَحِث or حَفِث.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state or condition of being a slave; slavery or servitude.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This denotes a status or condition, distinct from the act of worship and from the individual slave.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Parties of people or horsemen going in every direction; dispersed groups.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural with no singular in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Diverse, far-extending roads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used chiefly with reference to dispersion and going away, not approach.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hills or hillocks of the kind called إكام or آكام.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported concrete geographical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom, the extremities of the buttocks on which someone passes while riding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Restricted to the cited idiomatic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relating to dispersed parties of people going in every direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective formed from the plural-only noun عَبَادِيد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A servant, in a reported secondary or tropical use.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This Classical use is kept distinct from the Quranic participial sense of worshipper.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron shovel or spade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete tool noun, plural مَعَابِد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, rendered submissive or tractable, trained, tarred, or affected with mange or scab.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions include a camel treated with tar, rendered submissive by treatment or disease, or set apart for anointing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ship or boat, tarred or smeared with fat or oil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived passive-participial use applied to a vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a road, beaten, trodden, or made easy by repeated travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a route frequently used by travelers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wooden pin, peg, or stake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun attested in poetry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, honored, cared for, and served.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is reported as a contrary application alongside the sense of being rendered submissive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel left unridden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-related passive-participial use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a stallion camel, excited by lust or vehemently lustful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Restricted to the cited application to a male camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a country or tract of land, without tracks, footprints, signs of a way, or water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical use describing unmarked or inaccessible land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place set apart for religious services, exercises, or acts of devotion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun derived from the devotional branch.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Proper-name usage is covered by the desert meaning.

cautions: The alternate interpretation of عَبُدَ الطَّاغُوتِ is retained as Quran-focused evidence, but Lane's historical citation is not treated as a modern surah:ayah location.

The Quranic expression العابدين in 43:81 has materially different reported interpretations, including worshippers and angry or disdainful rejecters; the ordinary worshipper sense remains the primary presentation.

The Quranic noun group combines singular and several plural patterns. The evidence reports a common distinction between عبيد for owned slaves and عباد for servants or worshippers of God, but also notes broader overlap in divine-genitive constructions.
